helperReviews.proof: Definitional change unfolds S and sampleSum to x↦Σ_i g(x i). For each universally bound i:Fin n, measurable_pi_apply i is measurable into Ω; hg.comp gives measurability of x↦g(x i). The generated finite-sum theorem specialized at ℝ and Finset.univ combines exactly this family. No coordinate is chosen, including n=0.

Definitional change unfolds Q and sampleEnergy to x↦Σ_i (g(x i))^(2:ℕ). Each coordinate composition is measurable; pow_const with natural exponent2 produces exactly the squared coordinate. The same generated finite-sum theorem applies to the previously frozen squareFamily. No extra moment or Ω topology enters.

Assume hnot:¬(M.real A≤1/4). Real linear order yields 1/4<M.real A. sub_pos yields 0<M.real A−1/4, and hH:0<H gives hprod:0<H*(M.real A−1/4). hMarkA:H*M.real A≤N and hQuarter:H*(1/4)=N imply H*(M.real A−1/4)=H*M.real A−N≤0 after distributivity, contradicting hprod. nlinarith only receives these exact three facts.

Assume hnot:¬(M.real C≤1/4). Then 1/4<M.real C, so 0<M.real C−1/4 and hH makes hprod:0<H*(M.real C−1/4). The existing hMarkC:H*M.real C≤N together with hQuarter gives H*(M.real C−1/4)=H*M.real C−N≤0. This contradicts the positive product using the displayed nlinarith-only inputs. A and C are not confused; no independence or division is used.

B unfolds to the original conjunction |S x|≤2*sqrt N and Q x≤4*N. continuous_abs is specialized at ℝ; its measurability composes with hSMeas on Fin n→Ω. Both thresholds are real constant functions, hence measurable. measurableSet_le yields the two original non-strict comparison sets, whose intersection is definitionally the conjunction event. No topology or standard-Borel assumption on Ω and no strict-boundary/threshold change is introduced.
